# Handbook traceability matrix

Maps every `##` section of the [engineering handbook](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/README.md) onto the `*-audit` skill family. Source of truth: [`handbook-traceability.yaml`](handbook-traceability.yaml). Issue: lidia-tech/lidia-agents#543.

Section links are absolute GitHub URLs because the audit skills ship as a Claude Code plugin and run against other repositories, where a relative path out of the skill directory resolves to nothing.

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `static` | Statically auditable from a repo snapshot; mapped to a skill check or carries a gap entry. |
| `artifact` | Auditable only via artifacts (eval runs, CI history, issue/PR trail). Absence of the artifact is itself a finding - never a pass. |
| `process` | Process/culture; not verifiable from the repo. Audit-report prose and adoption recommendations, never fake-automated. |
| `informative` | Non-normative (spine, coda, symptom index); accounted for, maps to nothing. |

| Severity | Violating the clause means | Test |
|---|---|---|
| `critical` | Exposure that is hard to undo or reaches beyond the team: credentials or personal data leaked, licence or legal exposure, data loss, wrong output shipped to users unnoticed. | Could this appear in an incident report or a legal review? |
| `important` | You can still ship, but you can no longer tell whether what you shipped is right: silent incorrectness, unreproducible results, undiagnosable production failure, unbounded cost. | Does ignoring it destroy your ability to know the system works? |
| `minor` | Comfort, tidiness, or local velocity, with no effect on correctness, safety, or measurability. | Is the worst case "mildly annoying" or "harder to read"? |

Severity is orthogonal to class: class is *can we check it*, severity is *how bad if it is violated*. The scale is audit-core's own Critical / Important / Minor, so a matrix row and an audit finding speak the same language. Six notes govern how to read the column - the first two are interpretation rules, the rest explain splits a reader would otherwise take for errors:

**Baseline, not verdict.** A row records the severity a violation *inherently* carries, independent of any repo's current state. An auditor may raise or lower it for a specific instance with a stated reason - a load-bearing production prompt and a throwaway eval prompt violate the same clause at different cost.

**`process` rows carry a severity too.** "Spec before code" cannot be checked from a snapshot but is not thereby harmless, and an adoption roadmap needs to know what to sequence first. Only `informative` rows have none.

**Band counts per part do not rank the parts.** A part's distribution reflects how its clauses are cut into rows as much as what it is about: where a section bundles a consequential clause with hygiene, the row takes the higher band and the hygiene becomes invisible, so a part whose sections cut single-clause rows shows Minors that an otherwise similar part does not. Read the severity column per row, not per part.

**Documentation-currency clauses sit in different bands on purpose.** A currency clause is `important` when the stale claim is the reader's only access to the truth, and `minor` when the truth sits beside the claim: the prose tree exists to be read *instead of* the source, so a false claim in it is unfalsifiable where it is read, while a docstring or a commit-message rationale is read *beside* the artifact it describes and its staleness surfaces at the call site.

**Gate-shaped clauses land in more than one band.** A gate is rated on the harm it is the sole detector for, not on the subject it guards: encoding a class of security fix as a CI gate is `important` because the fixes themselves are the Critical part and the gate is one step removed, while a link-and-index checker guards a `minor` property and stays there.

**A checklist recap inherits its band.** A recap row takes the maximum severity of everything it recaps, so it adds no risk surface of its own. Where one lands in the Critical band, it points at rows already in the list rather than widening it, so a triager should read past it to the rows it recaps.

Each row's first cell links to the handbook section and restates the claim the row covers; where one section's claims fall into different classes or map to different skills, the row is split and the split is marked `(a)`, `(b)`, ... The **Notes** column carries the row's rationale - why a class was chosen, what a mapping reaches, what it deliberately leaves to the gap.

## Maintenance rules

Two rules keep the walk reproducible. Apply them when adding or revising a row.

**Gap taxonomy.** `extend-skill` when an existing skill is the natural owner and the fix is one new check record inside it - or a declaration of coverage it already has outside its check records. `new-domain` when no existing skill is a natural owner and the capability itself is missing; a note that says the claim "belongs to the domain the target issue creates" is `new-domain`, never `extend-skill`. `report-only` when the claim is auditable but belongs in report prose against the handbook's own checklist rather than in any skill's matrix. Every `extend-skill` gap names its owning skill in the note; every `new-domain` gap carries the issue that would create the domain, or says explicitly that none exists yet.

**Near-miss mappings.** Map a check that only partly reaches a claim when it would *flag* the handbook's violation, and record the residue as a gap on the same row. Refuse it - and gap the whole claim - when it would *pass* the violation. Worked example: an inline hard-coded model ID is more pinned than an alias, so `eval/reproducibility` is satisfied by exactly what Part 5 forbids; that row maps nothing and gaps everything.

| [Coding-hygiene rules that surface at review](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/implementation-disciplines.md#coding-hygiene-rules-that-surface-at-review) (c)<br>Commit no environment-specific values - no personal absolute paths, account or profile names, or hostnames in code, docs, or scripts - use placeholders and say what they resolve to, and fix them retroactively when touching a file that has them. | static | Important | - | **extend-skill** - security-audit is the owner, since its `security/secrets-in-code` pass already walks every literal in the tree, but that check is scoped to credentials and a personal path or profile name is a portability leak rather than a secret, so nothing scans for one. | - |
| [Coding-hygiene rules that surface at review](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/implementation-disciplines.md#coding-hygiene-rules-that-surface-at-review) (d)<br>Describe every settings field, keep module docstrings current with the module's purpose and interface, and prefer explicit enums or non-null defaults for agent tool parameters where the provider handles nullable arguments poorly. | static | Minor | - | **extend-skill** - docstring currency is exactly docs/docstring-staleness's own near miss: that check's detection is contradiction (a docstring actively wrong about parameters, return type, or behaviour), while this claim's 'current with purpose and interface' ask is broader - a docstring left incomplete after a change (a new parameter added but not yet mentioned) contradicts nothing and passes the check while still failing the ask. Not a duplicate of ci-and-static-analysis-b or documentation/keep-the-living-docs-current-too-a despite the shared clause: the two claims either side of it, self-documenting settings fields and provider-safe tool-argument types, have no check anywhere. | - |

## Part 3: Codebase structure

| Section / claim | Class | Severity | Mapped checks | Gap | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Order the tiers by reuse](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#order-the-tiers-by-reuse)<br>Sort the code by how much of it carries over to the next agent or task and let dependencies run only from the task-shaped code toward the reusable core, never the other way and never in a cycle; each project picks its own tier list, the ordering principle being what matters, and the handbook's typical layering runs shared schemas and types, core infrastructure, configuration, external integrations, capabilities, evaluation, then agents and applications. | static | Minor | `arch/layering` / Layering / dependency-rule conformance<br>`arch/cycles` / Cycles | - | arch-audit's `arch/layering` check is explicitly at its strongest when the project documents its tiers, so it audits conformance to whichever tier list the project declares. What it does not second-guess is the ordering principle behind that list - sort by reuse - which is a design judgment rather than a graph property. |
| [Point every dependency toward the core, and never cycle](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#point-every-dependency-toward-the-core-and-never-cycle) (a)<br>Hold one invariant - an import may only point at a more-reusable tier than the one it lives in, and the graph has no cycles - so core infrastructure never imports an application's types, and cross-application reuse goes through composition (exposing one agent to another as a tool) rather than reaching into another application's internals. | static | Important | `arch/layering` / Layering / dependency-rule conformance<br>`arch/cycles` / Cycles | - | - |
| [Point every dependency toward the core, and never cycle](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#point-every-dependency-toward-the-core-and-never-cycle) (b)<br>Write the project's tier-import rule down explicitly, which tier may import which, so it is enforceable by an import-boundary linter in CI rather than by memory. | static | Minor | `ci/gate-enforcement` / Gate enforcement | **extend-skill** - arch-audit is the owner, but its `arch/layering` check presupposes that the project has documented its tiers rather than asking whether it has, and no check looks for an import-boundary contract at all; ci-audit's `ci/gate-enforcement` reaches only the case where such a workflow already exists and asks whether it is required. | - |
| [Why the rule matters](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#why-the-rule-matters) (a)<br>Keep a convenience that a single application needs inside that application rather than migrating it down into the core, where it would bake one workflow's assumptions into shared code and couple every other consumer to them. | static | Important | `arch/over-abstraction` / Over-abstraction / speculative generality | **extend-skill** - partial - arch-audit is the owner, and its `arch/over-abstraction` check reaches the migrated convenience only while it still has a single consumer, and what it measures there is the unused generality rather than the coupling. The case the handbook warns about hardest, a core convenience that has since acquired a second consumer and now binds both to one workflow's assumptions, reads as justified generality to that check and is invisible to every other one. | Mapped through the check's one-consumer tell - a shared unit whose anticipated second caller never arrived - which is a real but partial reach; the residue is recorded as the gap above. |
| [Why the rule matters](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#why-the-rule-matters) (b)<br>Read an import that would violate the rule as a design smell rather than a lint nuisance - the concept is in the wrong tier, or it is two concepts that need splitting - which is how the shape pays off in independently testable tiers, local churn and an integration tax paid once. | process | Minor | - | - | What a team does with a flagged import - relocate the concept, split it, or silence the rule - is a disposition the repo never records, and the three payoffs are explanatory prose. |
| [Watch for structural decay beyond layering](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#watch-for-structural-decay-beyond-layering)<br>Periodically measure the declared architecture against the real import graph and watch five further decay signals - cycles (a warning within a package, a real break across one), coupling and cohesion (hub modules and grab-bag utils, split along cohesion seams), complexity, dead code (verified truly unreachable before deletion), and outsized files - as health signals rather than absolutes. | static | Important | `arch/layering` / Layering / dependency-rule conformance<br>`arch/cycles` / Cycles<br>`arch/coupling` / Coupling & cohesion<br>`arch/complexity` / Complexity<br>`arch/dead-code` / Dead code<br>`arch/size` / File / module size | - | The closest section-to-skill fit anywhere in the handbook - arch declares a check for every signal named here, and adds `arch/hidden-coupling` for the edges an import graph misses and `arch/over-decomposition` for the opposite fault, neither of which this section names. The cadence ("periodically") is process, and the closing pointer to an import-linter contract in CI is carried by point-every-dependency-toward-the-core-and-never-cycle-b. |
| [Compose agents with typed hooks over a generic runner](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#compose-agents-with-typed-hooks-over-a-generic-runner) (a)<br>Don't fork a base agent - give the core tier a generic runner that owns the run lifecycle and exposes a small set of hook methods (create the agent, build the collector, format the query, post-process the result), customize each application by overriding those hooks, and narrow the runner's loose metadata into typed sub-models so run records are self-describing. | static | Minor | - | **extend-skill** - arch-audit is the nearest owner, but no check detects plumbing duplicated once per application - the tell is repetition across agents, not a bad import - and its axes point the other way, since a generic runner with one implementer reads as `arch/over-abstraction`, so composition-over-forking stays invisible until the fork produces a cycle or a layering break. | - |
| [Compose agents with typed hooks over a generic runner](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#compose-agents-with-typed-hooks-over-a-generic-runner) (b)<br>Build multi-agent systems by exposing one agent to another as a tool, the only sanctioned cross-application dependency, and design the split so it reflects a genuine data dependency between sub-agents rather than an arbitrary partition. | static | Important | `arch/layering` / Layering / dependency-rule conformance | **extend-skill** - arch-audit is the owner - the as_tool rule is a dependency-rule question it can already see, and a spurious sub-agent boundary is a decomposition defect `arch/over-decomposition` is the right lens for. What that check reads today is the module import graph, not the agent-composition graph, so whether a split corresponds to a real hand-off is invisible; the fix is to extend that check to the second graph. | - |
| [Dispatch on a discriminator, not a type](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#dispatch-on-a-discriminator-not-a-type)<br>Select interchangeable backends through a polymorphic configuration - a base config carrying a mode discriminator, each concrete variant in its own module, dispatch by match or switch on the discriminator literal and never by a runtime type test - with a settings library resolving environment variables per variant and one provider-agnostic entry point returning a uniform result type. | static | Minor | `arch/layering` / Layering / dependency-rule conformance | **extend-skill** - arch-audit is the owner, and the row maps only on the consequence the handbook names, a type-test chain that couples the dispatcher to every concrete class and so breaks a tier boundary; no check flags isinstance/instanceof dispatch as such, nor asks for a single provider-agnostic entry point or declarative per-variant settings resolution. The section is written from a Python vantage (Pydantic discriminated unions, match on a Literal, pydantic-settings per variant); the equivalent TypeScript shape - a discriminated union on a literal tag, switch with exhaustiveness checking, and a schema library resolving env per variant - needs confirming before this row is audited on a TS codebase (#5). | - |
| [Name every configuration worth reusing](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#name-every-configuration-worth-reusing)<br>Treat a configuration as the full bundle that pins a run - model, its parameters, tool and feature toggles, budgets and limits - and give any combination worth reusing a name as a machine-readable profile, selectable by name and discoverable by listing, so scripts, eval harnesses and agents reference it by name instead of reconstructing a pile of flags per call site. | static | Important | - | **extend-skill** - eval-audit is the owner, and its `eval/reproducibility` check is the nearest existing one but asks only that a run's config be recorded, which a reconstructed flag pile satisfies; nothing asks whether reusable configurations are named, listable and referenced by name. Part 5's bundle-configuration-into-named-profiles carries the same claim from the harness side. | - |
| [Checklist: placing new code / reviewing an import](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#checklist-placing-new-code--reviewing-an-import)<br>Seven-item recap for placing code or reviewing an import - most reusable tier that fully contains the concerns, every import pointing at a more-reusable tier, no new cycle, single-application conveniences left in place, cross-application reuse by composition, discriminator dispatch, and the layering rule enforced by an import-linter contract in CI. | process | Important | - | - | A recap, so what it adds is the act of working the list at review time. Each of the seven items is owned by a Part 3 row above. |

## Part 4: The three-layer document model

| Section / claim | Class | Severity | Mapped checks | Gap | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [A document has no privileged decomposition](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/three-layer-model.md#a-document-has-no-privileged-decomposition)<br>Resist modelling a document type once and reusing that schema forever - importance is relative to the question, so no view-from-nowhere schema exists - while conceding that the reusable core is real, since intrinsic structure fully generalizes and a thin vocabulary of domain entities partially does, leaving only the task decomposition use-relative. | process | Minor | - | - | The premise of the part - a modelling stance about where generality is real - which no snapshot can date. Its operational form, three explicit layers with different reuse profiles, is carried by the rows below. |
| [Know the three layers](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/three-layer-model.md#know-the-three-layers)<br>Split document knowledge into three layers with distinct reuse profiles and epistemic status - Layer 1 intrinsic structure (fully reusable, perception), Layer 2 domain entities (partially reusable, grounding), Layer 3 workflow knowledge (not reusable, inference) - a decomposition that is domain-general rather than domain-specific. | static | Important | - | **report-only** - whether a document system's data model separates the three layers is visible in a snapshot, but no check owns it - arch-audit's `arch/layering` check reads module tiers, not data layers, and mapping this to it would audit the wrong graph. An auditor diagnoses it in report prose against Part 4's checklist. | - |
| [Never skip a layer](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/three-layer-model.md#never-skip-a-layer)<br>Never put the raw document into the prompt and ask the final Layer-3 question directly - the shortcut collapses three distinct error sites into one opaque call, so a failure stops being localizable to a layer - noting that re-reading a span the lower layers point at is navigation rather than skipping, and re-explaining the rule at the code review of every new agent. | static | Important | - | **report-only** - a pipeline that dumps a raw document into the final prompt is visible in a snapshot, yet no check audits it; prompt-audit's `prompt/grounding` is the nearest and asks whether the prompt supplies the context the task needs, never whether that context arrived through the lower layers. The review-ritual clause is process. | - |
| [Hold the contracts that make layering pay off](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/three-layer-model.md#hold-the-contracts-that-make-layering-pay-off) (a)<br>Make Layer 1 a single engine-agnostic representation - typed blocks, a containment hierarchy, provenance on every block, engine identity in the metadata rather than in the block shape - populated by a thin per-engine builder, with everything downstream reading the representation and never a raw engine output. | static | Minor | `arch/layering` / Layering / dependency-rule conformance | **extend-skill** - arch-audit is the owner of the anti-corruption boundary, a dependency rule (only the builder may import an engine's schema) it enforces once the project declares it among its layering rules. The representation's own requirements - typed blocks, containment, per-block provenance, engine identity kept out of the block shape - are schema properties no check inspects and no skill is a natural owner of, exactly as on hold-the-contracts-that-make-layering-pay-off-b; that residue is report prose against Part 4's checklist. | - |
| [Hold the contracts that make layering pay off](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/three-layer-model.md#hold-the-contracts-that-make-layering-pay-off) (b)<br>Hold the three remaining contracts - derive every block id from content rather than position, canonicalizing before hashing and treating cross-engine stability as an alignment problem rather than a property of the hash; run refinements as versioned, additive passes over an immutable base, keyed by those ids and stamped with implementation and version; and keep Layer 2 to task-independent domain facts while task-shaped judgments stay in each workflow's Layer 3. | static | Important | - | **report-only** - identity stability, additive enrichment over an immutable base, and the Layer-2/Layer-3 boundary are document-model design contracts with no check anywhere; the closest analogue is arch-audit's `arch/over-abstraction` check reading the same keep-the-core-sparse rule in the module graph (Part 3's why-the-rule-matters-a), which cannot see it in data. An auditor diagnoses these against Part 4's checklist in report prose. | - |
| [Compose typed tools over one fuzzy lookup](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/three-layer-model.md#compose-typed-tools-over-one-fuzzy-lookup)<br>Give an agent precise, typed operations over a layered document - structural navigation, clause search, entity-in-context, and semantic search over clean anchored units, each optionally following resolved references - instead of one similarity search, make choosing and composing the right tool the agent's job, and rest every tool on identifiers that survive re-extraction. | static | Important | - | **report-only** - no skill audits the shape of an agent's tool surface; eval-audit's `eval/prompt-quality` reaches tools only as drift between a prompt and the tools that exist, and prompt-audit judges the text of a prompt rather than what it is given to call. An auditor diagnoses the tool surface in report prose against Part 4's checklist, as on the other Part 4 rows. | - |
| [Why this is the organizing principle, not just a document feature](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/three-layer-model.md#why-this-is-the-organizing-principle-not-just-a-document-feature)<br>Keep the reusable core sparse and stable and the task layer rich and disposable is the document-model rule and the module-dependency rule at once, and because the layers are separable they are separately evaluable - a golden dataset per layer instead of one ill-defined end-to-end number. | static | Important | `eval/coverage` / Eval coverage | - | Mapped on the per-layer dataset claim, the document-side twin of Part 7's unit-by-unit rule - a layer visible only inside an end-to-end score is an uncovered capability. The code-shape half is Part 3's rows. |
| [Checklist: reviewing a document capability](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/three-layer-model.md#checklist-reviewing-a-document-capability)<br>Six-item recap for reviewing a document capability - the Layer-3 answer reached through Layers 1 and 2, downstream code reading the engine-agnostic representation, content-derived ids with alignment across engines, versioned additive passes over an immutable base, Layer 2 holding only task-independent facts, and a failure localizable to one separately evaluable layer. | process | Important | - | - | A recap, so what it adds is the act of working the list at the review of a document capability. Each of the six items is owned by a Part 4 row above. |
| [See also](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/three-layer-model.md#see-also)<br>Cross-links to Parts 3 and 7 and the handbook index. | informative | - | - | - | - |

## Part 5: The extended agent harness

| Section / claim | Class | Severity | Mapped checks | Gap | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Build the harness, don't inline the plumbing](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#build-the-harness-dont-inline-the-plumbing)<br>Solve model access, configuration, headless execution and reliability once in the shared core and configuration tiers instead of wiring them into each agent module, so the marginal agent is mostly its prompt and its tools, and put the production-reliability decisions in the harness so bounding is the default rather than an afterthought each author reinvents. | static | Minor | - | **extend-skill** - arch-audit is the nearest owner but has no check for plumbing duplicated once per agent - the tell is repetition across applications, not a bad import - and nothing audits which tier the reliability defaults live in; the bounding half of the claim is carried by make-bounding-the-default. | - |
| [Resolve models through aliases, never hard-coded IDs](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#resolve-models-through-aliases-never-hard-coded-ids)<br>Never name a concrete provider model inline - take a short alias whose prefix encodes the provider and resolve it through a central catalog that stays the single place knowing real model IDs, regions and credentials - so switching the model a run uses is a one-token change and screening a dozen candidates never touches the agent. | static | Minor | - | **extend-skill** - eval-audit is the owner, since model identity is its surface, but no check scans call sites for inline provider model IDs; its `eval/reproducibility` check is the nearest and wants a run's model version pinned and recorded, which an inline ID satisfies perfectly well - the worked example of the near-miss rule, mapping it would pass exactly what the handbook forbids - and security-audit's `security/secrets-in-code` sees only the credentials half of what the catalog centralizes. | - |
| [Expose model parameters as optional, defaulted flags](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#expose-model-parameters-as-optional-defaulted-flags)<br>Make generation parameters (temperature, top-p, penalties) optional flags that fall back to provider defaults, expose reasoning or extended thinking as a budget flag where the model supports it, and settle whether any such change is an improvement as a hypothesis measured against a frozen benchmark, one variable at a time. | static | Minor | - | **extend-skill** - eval-audit is the owner, since the generation-parameter surface is exactly what a like-for-like comparison varies one variable at a time, but the section's own claim is wholly unmapped - no check asks whether generation parameters are exposed as optional flags falling back to provider defaults, nor whether a reasoning budget flag exists where the model supports one. | The closing clause - treat a parameter change as a hypothesis measured against a frozen benchmark, one variable at a time - is a cross-reference to Part 7 and is already owned there, split across two rows - the one-variable-at-a-time half by evaluation/measure-honestly-c, which classes it artifact and carries eval-audit's `eval/methodology` and `eval/reproducibility`, and the frozen-benchmark half by evaluation/build-a-dataset-you-can-trust. This row keeps only the harness-side claim, the same division offer-cheap-and-mock-backends uses for its Part 7 clauses. |
| [Bundle configuration into named profiles](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#bundle-configuration-into-named-profiles)<br>Have the configuration tier bundle a model, its parameters and feature toggles into a named profile that is selectable by name, discoverable by listing and machine-readable, so scripts and eval harnesses reference a configuration by name and "run the cheap profile" becomes an unambiguous shared instruction. | static | Important | - | **extend-skill** - the same unmapped claim and the same owner as Part 3's name-every-configuration-worth-reusing, stated from the harness side - eval-audit's `eval/reproducibility` is the nearest existing check and is satisfied by a recorded flag pile, and no check asks for named, listable, machine-readable profiles. | - |
| [Ship every agent with a headless CLI](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#ship-every-agent-with-a-headless-cli)<br>Give every agent a headless command-line entry point that takes a query and writes its artifacts to an output directory, make it the same path an eval harness drives as a subprocess so no separate eval mode can diverge from production, land artifacts in a dated subfolder that names what produced the run, and build any interactive UI as that CLI's peer rather than a second implementation. | static | Important | - | **extend-skill** - eval-audit is the owner, because this is the precondition for its entire evidence base and an eval driving a code path production never takes is a validity threat next door to `eval/contamination`; still, no check asks whether a headless artifact-producing entry point exists, whether the eval path is the production path, or whether run artifacts are named and kept so a result stays findable months later. | - |
| [Offer cheap and mock backends: a fast inner loop is a discipline](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#offer-cheap-and-mock-backends-a-fast-inner-loop-is-a-discipline)<br>Offer cheaper flag-selected backends - a mock backend such as a small model over a fixed knowledge base, or a lighter real one for the same capability - that keep the loop fast without changing the agent, treat the cheap inner loop as a first-class capability because it is what buys a variance band instead of an anecdote, and compare backends on full cost including the downstream context a stand-in inflates. | static | Important | `eval/regression-tracking` / Regression tracking & cost | - | `eval/regression-tracking` names a cheap/mock eval mode outright, so this is the most direct mapping in Part 5. The two clauses it does not reach inherit gaps already recorded in Part 7 - the variance band on evaluation/measure-honestly-a (#3) and full-cost accounting on evaluation/measure-honestly-b (#2). |
| [Make bounding the default](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#make-bounding-the-default)<br>Bake six reliability defaults into the harness rather than into each agent - wall-clock and idle timeouts on turns and streaming loops, a hardened outbound HTTP client (explicit connect and read timeouts, bounded retries, keep-alive) whose retries wrap only operations safe to repeat, a circuit breaker on a dependency that keeps failing, a cycle and token budget cap on the agent loop, a size strategy for oversized tool results, and time-bounded teardown of external resources - because an unbounded call, cycle or payload each exhaust a resource. | static | Critical | - | **new-domain** - #2 - production-reliability bounding has no owner anywhere in the family - not one of the eight skills declares a check for timeouts, retry safety, circuit breakers, loop or payload caps. The planned performance/cost and observability lenses in #2 are the nearest: they would see the symptoms (a hung run, an unattributed spend, an undiagnosable failure) but their stated scope is measurement and diagnosability, not the harness-level bounds that prevent them. Folded into #2 by decision on 2026-07-29, widening that issue from measuring the symptom to auditing the bound - the alternative, a ninth reliability domain, would split one dependency call between two lenses. | - |
| [Checklist: standing up a new agent](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#checklist-standing-up-a-new-agent)<br>Eight-item recap for standing up an agent - model alias through the catalog, optional defaulted parameter flags, a named profile, a headless CLI that is the eval path, dated self-describing artifact folders, a flag-selectable cheap or mock backend, time-bounded external calls with retries only on repeatable operations, and bounded loop, payload and failing dependencies. | process | Critical | - | - | A recap, so what it adds is the act of working the list when a new agent is stood up. Each of the eight items is owned by a Part 5 row above. |
| [See also](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#see-also)<br>Cross-links to Parts 3, 6 and 7 and the handbook index. | informative | - | - | - | - |

## Part 6: Observability

| Section / claim | Class | Severity | Mapped checks | Gap | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Instrument before you tune](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/observability.md#instrument-before-you-tune)<br>Make the first move on any performance question adding the per-item metadata that measures what happens rather than running a parameter sweep, look upstream of the part you were about to optimize because the highest-leverage intervention frequently sits there, and distrust averages, since a healthy-looking overall number can mask a bimodal split whose real win is eliminating the low mode at its source. | process | Important | - | - | The section's own claim is the order of moves in an investigation - instrument, then tune - which no snapshot can date. The instrumentation it demands is carried by capture-per-subagent-per-tool-usage. |
| [Keep observability out of the model's context](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/observability.md#keep-observability-out-of-the-models-context)<br>Send analysis metadata through a side channel the model never sees - persist per-item timing, sizes, utilization and cost alongside the run in its artifacts rather than inside the prompt, and attach any bookkeeping a tool must carry to a metadata envelope the downstream code consumes rather than to the tool output the model reads. | static | Important | `prompt/grounding` / Grounding & handling the unknown | **new-domain** - #2 - mapped only where the metadata is visible in the prompt text, which `prompt/grounding` flags as a pile of context the task does not need; the side channel itself - a metadata envelope consumed by downstream code and persisted into the run artifacts - is a runtime data path no check inspects. | - |
| [Capture per-(sub)agent, per-tool usage](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/observability.md#capture-per-subagent-per-tool-usage)<br>Have the run harness produce a typed per-(sub)agent and per-tool usage record - tokens including cache read and write, wall-clock timing, agent-loop cycles, and per-tool total time and cost - so that utilization (how much of everything fetched actually informed the answer) and the stage a multi-agent run spends its time in both become visible. | static | Important | - | **new-domain** - #2 - not one of the eight skills declares a check for run instrumentation; eval-audit's `eval/regression-tracking` is the nearest and asks whether eval results are tracked over time and cheap to produce, never whether a run emits a per-agent, per-tool usage record at all. | - |
| [Account for the full cost, not the convenient part](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/observability.md#account-for-the-full-cost-not-the-convenient-part)<br>Take cost from actual billing rather than estimating it from token counts, count cache read and write tokens, sub-agent calls, latency and retries, price a component by its effect on the whole pipeline rather than by its local price, pair every efficiency number with an independent quality evaluation, and lead with absolute figures over percentages. | artifact | Important | `eval/methodology` / Methodology soundness | **extend-skill** - #2 - the pairing clause is mapped because an efficiency number reported on its own is exactly the gameable proxy `eval/methodology` exists to catch; full-cost accounting is the same unmapped claim recorded on evaluation/measure-honestly-b, stated here from the observability side, and the target issue is the cost domain whose accounting rules the new eval-audit check should reuse. | - |
| [Make errors diagnosable](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/observability.md#make-errors-diagnosable)<br>Swallow no exception - report each to the downstream consumer with its type and message at minimum, log it at the right level where it is actually visible during debugging, or re-raise it for a better-positioned caller - so the error message alone says what went wrong without reproducing the issue, a generic internal-error string being the opposite of observability. | static | Important | `security/sensitive-data` / Sensitive-data handling | **new-domain** - #2 - the same division and the same recommendation as Part 2's coding-hygiene row, which states this rule as a review rule - security-audit reaches only the broad handlers that hide a security failure, and the developer-facing half, an exception collapsed into a generic string carrying neither type nor message, belongs to the observability domain the target issue creates. | - |
| [Close the loop: production → development](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/observability.md#close-the-loop-production--development)<br>Persist the same per-(sub)agent usage record with each production interaction so a real-world session can be triaged after the fact - where a turn spent its time, whether it hung or merely ran long, which tool errored - because instrumentation that persists into production artifacts is what lets you debug the run you were not watching. | static | Important | - | **new-domain** - #2 - no check asks whether instrumentation reaches the production path; every skill's evidence base stops at the repo and at eval runs, so a project whose dev runs are fully instrumented and whose production interactions record nothing passes each existing check. | - |
| [Checklist: instrumenting a run](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/observability.md#checklist-instrumenting-a-run)<br>Eight-item recap for instrumenting a run - per-(sub)agent and per-tool usage recorded with cache read/write tokens, timing, loop cycles and per-tool cost, a typed record rather than a loose dict, analysis metadata on a side channel, utilization captured, cost from actual billing with the whole-pipeline effect included, every efficiency number paired with a quality number, no swallowed exceptions, and the same record persisted into production artifacts. | process | Important | - | - | A recap, so what it adds is the act of working the list when a run is instrumented. Each of the eight items is owned by a Part 6 row above. |
| [See also](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/observability.md#see-also)<br>Cross-links to Parts 2, 5, 7 and 10 and the handbook index. | informative | - | - | - | - |

## Part 7: Evaluation

| Section / claim | Class | Severity | Mapped checks | Gap | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [The enemy is false confidence](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#the-enemy-is-false-confidence)<br>Treat every non-trivial change as a hypothesis and keep the decision falsifiable - the dataset and the metric must exist before the decision they settle. | process | Important | - | - | The ordering (yardstick before decision) is not datable from a snapshot; its auditable residue - gold independence and a frozen dataset - is carried by the build-a-dataset-you-can-trust row. |
| [Run the loop](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#run-the-loop) (a)<br>Run the loop and do not stop at shipping - re-measure afterwards, because the change surfaces new failure forms that become the next dataset extension. | process | Important | - | - | Whether anyone re-measured after shipping is an act, not a repo state - a dataset that grew could equally be routine curation. The residue it leaves, the decision and its evidence written where the next person finds them, is carried by the -b row. |
| [Run the loop](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#run-the-loop) (b)<br>Record each decision and its evidence where the next person can find it. | artifact | Important | `eval/regression-tracking` / Regression tracking & cost | - | - |
| [Measure the behaviors that matter](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#measure-the-behaviors-that-matter) (a)<br>Enumerate the behaviors the product depends on - accuracy, grounding, format, refusals, latency and cost, the specific failure modes, and adversarial injection-resistance - and map each to an eval, because an unevaluated capability is an unmonitored one. | static | Important | `eval/coverage` / Eval coverage<br>`eval/prompt-quality` / Prompt / SOP quality | - | - |
| [Measure the behaviors that matter](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#measure-the-behaviors-that-matter) (b)<br>Match the grader to the behavior - code-graded assertions, judge-graded rubrics, and trajectory graders that assert on the path the run took rather than only on its answer. | static | Important | `eval/methodology` / Methodology soundness | **extend-skill** - eval-audit is the owner, and its `eval/methodology` check reaches the wrong-grader case as "a metric that is a gameable proxy", but it never asks which grader *type* the behavior needs, and trajectory grading - asserting on the path a run took rather than on its answer - is unrepresented anywhere in the family. | - |
| [Build a dataset you can trust](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#build-a-dataset-you-can-trust)<br>Draw candidates from a source independent of the system under test, choose the dataset shape that supplies that independence, measure prevalence before planning the harvest, and freeze the set for the duration of a comparison. | static | Important | `eval/contamination` / Contamination / leakage<br>`eval/methodology` / Methodology soundness<br>`eval/reproducibility` / Reproducibility | - | - |
| [Measure honestly](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#measure-honestly) (a)<br>A single run of a stochastic system is an anecdote - run each candidate several times and report the spread, per-case k-of-N reliability bands and the strict pass^N aggregate. | artifact | Important | - | **extend-skill** - #3 - no eval-audit check requires repeated runs or a reported variance band; the target issue exists to add exactly this one. | - |
| [Measure honestly](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#measure-honestly) (b)<br>Settle quality/cost trade-offs on full cost taken from actual billing - cache read/write tokens, sub-agent calls, latency and retries included - and lead with absolute figures. | artifact | Important | - | **extend-skill** - #2 - extend eval-audit - its `eval/regression-tracking` check is about the cost of running evals, not about pricing a candidate comparison honestly; the target issue is the cost domain whose accounting rules the new eval-audit check should reuse, not itself the thing being extended. | - |
| [Measure honestly](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#measure-honestly) (c)<br>Keep comparisons like-for-like by changing one variable at a time, bucket refusals and API errors apart from quality failures, and make every reported number regenerable from a pinned model, a recorded config and kept artifacts. | artifact | Important | `eval/methodology` / Methodology soundness<br>`eval/reproducibility` / Reproducibility | - | - |
| [Pick the approach that fits the decision](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#pick-the-approach-that-fits-the-decision)<br>Match the approach to the decision's shape - screening funnel, blind paired A/B, ground-truth evaluation, anchor-based recall probe, golden-set benchmark - and reach for the cheapest that actually answers your question. | static | Important | - | **extend-skill** - eval-audit is the owner, and none of its checks asks whether the eval approach fits the decision it settles, nor whether expensive semantic scoring is staged behind cheap deterministic gates. | - |
| [Grow the eval into a gate](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#grow-the-eval-into-a-gate)<br>An eval earns merge-blocking authority in rungs - offline, then shadow mode on production traffic, then a required CI gate - and a miss it lets through becomes a new case in the dataset. | static | Important | `eval/smoke-test-gate` / Smoke-test gate<br>`ci/gate-enforcement` / Gate enforcement | **extend-skill** - the middle rung - "run it in shadow mode on production traffic, blocking nothing, before it can block a merge" - has no check anywhere; eval-audit is the owner, and its `eval/smoke-test-gate` covers only the promoted, merge-blocking end of the ladder. | - |
| [Use the LLM judge only where it agrees with the human](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#use-the-llm-judge-only-where-it-agrees-with-the-human)<br>Trust an LLM judge only on the dimensions where measured human correlation shows it tracks the expert, pair efficiency metrics with an independent quality measure, and treat a gold label as a revisable verdict rather than bedrock. | artifact | Important | `eval/methodology` / Methodology soundness | - | - |
| [Ask for a described category, not a bare number](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#ask-for-a-described-category-not-a-bare-number)<br>Where the model itself returns a judgment, ask for a point on a small closed scale whose every point carries a described trigger and keep free numbers for quantities the model did not self-report, because verbalized confidence clusters on a few round anchors, a bare number invites a threshold nobody argued for, and only a described anchor gives two raters the same referent. | static | Important | `eval/verdict-scale` / Judge verdict scale (shape of the model's own judgment) | - | - |
| [Evaluate a multi-agent system unit by unit](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#evaluate-a-multi-agent-system-unit-by-unit)<br>Score a multi-agent system unit by unit, each against its own golden dataset and metric, instead of one end-to-end number that cannot say which unit failed. | static | Important | `eval/coverage` / Eval coverage | - | Mapped as coverage - a unit visible only inside an end-to-end score is an uncovered capability. The "units exposed as separately-runnable pieces" half of the claim belongs to the Part 3 and Part 5 rows. |
| [Build escalation ladders: spend measurement where it pays](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#build-escalation-ladders-spend-measurement-where-it-pays)<br>Let a cheap high-precision method settle the common case and escalate only the residual, with the precision/recall crossover located by measurement because a rule set is a precision floor, not a recall guarantee. | static | Important | - | **extend-skill** - eval-audit is the owner, and none of its checks asks whether a fast-path/escalation threshold was justified by an independent recall probe at the crossover rather than set by feel. | - |
| [Step-by-step: running an evaluation](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#step-by-step-running-an-evaluation)<br>Runbook for one evaluation - name the decision, establish and freeze an independent dataset, fix the harness, change one variable, run each candidate several times, score quality with full cost, calibrate the judge, then decide, record and re-measure. | process | Important | - | - | A procedure a snapshot cannot show was followed; each substantive step is mapped by the rows above. |
| [Name the anti-patterns out loud](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/evaluation.md#name-the-anti-patterns-out-loud)<br>Scan every result for the six named anti-patterns - grading your own homework, "we added more patterns", the single run, quality without cost, moving the goalposts mid-experiment, demo-driven selection. | artifact | Important | `eval/contamination` / Contamination / leakage<br>`eval/coverage` / Eval coverage<br>`eval/methodology` / Methodology soundness<br>`eval/reproducibility` / Reproducibility | - | Two of the six - the single run and quality without cost - inherit the gaps recorded on measure-honestly-a and measure-honestly-b. |

## Part 8: Documentation & knowledge capture

| Section / claim | Class | Severity | Mapped checks | Gap | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Aim for docs that stand alone; drifted docs are worse than none](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#aim-for-docs-that-stand-alone-drifted-docs-are-worse-than-none) (a)<br>Aim for docs that convey on their own what the system does and how it is built without reading the source, and hold every claim in them to the rule that governs a test - it must be verifiable and it must have been verified - because a drifted doc launders a stale belief into an authoritative-looking claim and so does more damage than a missing one, which makes finding and fixing a dead cross-link, an unresolvable import path or a renamed flag real work rather than tidying. | static | Important | `docs/coverage` / Coverage<br>`docs/cross-referencing` / Cross-referencing | **extend-skill** - docs-audit is the owner - its `docs/coverage` check reaches the stand-alone standard as a per-component documented/partial/gap status and `docs/cross-referencing` reaches the dead cross-link, but drift itself has no column - a doc that confidently describes a flag the code renamed is neither a missing doc nor a broken link, so the doc-versus-source comparison the skill's evidence pass builds has nowhere to land. | - |
| [Aim for docs that stand alone; drifted docs are worse than none](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#aim-for-docs-that-stand-alone-drifted-docs-are-worse-than-none) (b)<br>Move a change and its documentation together in the same pull request, not later. | artifact | Important | - | **new-domain** - #11 - whether a code change carried its doc update in the same pull request is delivery-trail evidence, and no skill in the family reads commit or pull-request history - the delivery-trail domain the target issue creates, which would hand docs-audit the code-only-PR signal. | - |
| [Keep the architecture-vs-research split](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#keep-the-architecture-vs-research-split)<br>Keep two kinds of writing distinct - architecture docs, prescriptive and describing what is actually implemented, and research docs, background investigation marked explicitly not authoritative - cross-link the two when an investigation lands in code instead of letting transcripts accumulate among the prescriptive docs, and organize the whole tree by audience and concern behind a navigable index every docs pull request keeps current. | static | Important | `docs/organization` / Organization<br>`docs/cross-referencing` / Cross-referencing | **extend-skill** - partial - docs-audit is the owner, the placement and cross-linking halves are covered exactly, but the section also requires a research doc to be marked explicitly not authoritative for current behaviour, and no check reads a doc's labelling; `docs/organization` sees only where a doc sits, so a correctly filed but unmarked research doc passes both cited checks. | The split is one of docs-audit's own standing rules and `docs/cross-referencing` names the background-to-prescriptive reciprocal link outright, so the fit is close to exact on placement and linkage. The labelling residue is recorded as the gap above rather than left in this note. |
| [Keep the decision-trail artifacts](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#keep-the-decision-trail-artifacts) (a)<br>Keep the six records that make a decision and its evidence survive the moment - the forward-looking spec, plan and ADR, and the backward-looking story, experiment write-up and results log - reserving the ADR for a decision meant to outlive both a spec and a story, leaving implementation-level rationale in the story, and never skipping the story, which holds the why and the surprises a diff cannot. | artifact | Important | `eval/regression-tracking` / Regression tracking & cost | **extend-skill** - mapped only on the results log, which is the leaderboard-or-history record that check asks for; docs-audit owns the rest as docs-tree artifacts, yet no check asks whether a piece of work left its spec, plan, ADR, story or experiment write-up - its `docs/coverage` check is per code component, not per decision - the same gap Part 1's step-by-step row records for the spec and the plan, and the per-change half of it needs the delivery-trail evidence base (#11). | - |
| [Keep the decision-trail artifacts](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#keep-the-decision-trail-artifacts) (b)<br>Treat the data model itself as a first-class context artifact alongside the decision trail - a versioned, explicit description of the schemas the system works over plus their known quirks and invariants, that both people and agents are pointed at - because an agent left to infer it from scattered code reinvents it wrong and an undocumented quirk is a bug waiting for the next author. | static | Important | `docs/coverage` / Coverage | **extend-skill** - partial - docs-audit is the owner, and its `docs/coverage` check reaches presence and depth (a schema surface with no dedicated doc is a gap row, one documented without its quirks and invariants lands as partial), but the section also requires the description to be versioned, and no check asks whether a doc carries a version that tracks the schema it describes. | - |
| [Audit docs like a test suite](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#audit-docs-like-a-test-suite) (a)<br>Run periodic passes that re-read the documentation against the source and fix what has drifted, along three axes - organization (misfiled, duplicated or deprecated content, and the shape of the tree), cross-referencing (every internal link resolving, no orphans, reciprocal links present) and coverage (each code component documented, partial or a gap) - because the value is not the tidy diff but the guarantee that every claim was checked against reality. | static | Important | `docs/organization` / Organization<br>`docs/cross-referencing` / Cross-referencing<br>`docs/coverage` / Coverage | - | The three axes named here are docs-audit's three checks, which makes this the closest section-to-skill fit in Part 8. The cadence ("periodic") is the same audit-cadence question Part 1's make-the-standard-executable row records as sitting outside every skill's evidence base. |
| [Audit docs like a test suite](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#audit-docs-like-a-test-suite) (b)<br>Wire a link-and-index checker into CI as the cheapest guardrail, so a dead link or an unindexed doc fails the build instead of rotting quietly. | static | Minor | `ci/gate-enforcement` / Gate enforcement | **extend-skill** - `ci/gate-enforcement` asks whether a checker that exists is actually required, so a project with no checker at all passes it; docs-audit is the owner and treats the checker as a deliverable it may propose rather than as a check it scores. | - |
| [Keep the living docs current too](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#keep-the-living-docs-current-too) (a)<br>Keep every module and public symbol carrying a docstring that says what it does and how to use it, updated whenever the purpose or interface changes and audited both ways, for coverage and for staleness, and route fixing one through the normal code gate rather than the lighter docs-only path. | static | Minor | - | **extend-skill** - This is the fullest of the three docstring rows, and each of its axes is a near miss to a different opt-in record. docs/docstring-standard checks conformance to 'the project's convention', a locally-defined bar that can be weaker than this claim's fixed 'what it does and how to use it' ask. docs/docstring-coverage and docs/docstring-staleness carry the same near misses as the other two docstring rows (an existence bar vs. the quality bar, and contradiction vs. the broader currency ask). Nothing checks whether a docstring fix that resolves one of these actually took the normal code gate rather than the lighter docs-only path. Third of the three docstring rows (with ci-and-static-analysis-b and coding-hygiene-rules-that-surface-at-review-d); the code-gate clause is unique to this row. | - |
| [Keep the living docs current too](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#keep-the-living-docs-current-too) (b)<br>Hold the coding rules, review thresholds and git workflow in the project's binding-rules file, the one the team and the coding agents both read as authoritative, and maintain it - where it and this handbook disagree, the rules file wins and the handbook is the bug. | static | Important | - | **extend-skill** - the same unmapped claim as the README's where-the-binding-rules-live row, stated from the documentation side - docs-audit is the owner and has no check for an authoritative rules file or for a doc-versus-doc contradiction, and ci-audit's `ci/gate-enforcement` reads that mismatch only for what the file claims CI enforces. | - |
| [Keep the living docs current too](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#keep-the-living-docs-current-too) (c)<br>Document a prompt or SOP change in its commit message with the why rather than only the what, and keep it in its own commit where you can. | artifact | Minor | - | **extend-skill** - the same unmapped claim and the same owners as Part 2's prompt-and-sop-engineering row - eval-audit's `eval/prompt-quality` owns prompt-change hygiene through its missing-versioning-or-changelog clause and prompt-audit states the convention in its own remediation section, but neither actually reads commit messages to verify it, which is the evidence base the delivery-trail domain (#11) would supply. | - |
| [Keep the living docs current too](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#keep-the-living-docs-current-too) (d)<br>Keep any generated diagram in a text metalanguage (Mermaid, PlantUML, D2) rather than a binary image and regenerate it from the source of truth on merge, so it cannot drift the way a hand-drawn or model-drawn one does and stays diffable in review like the rest of the source. | static | Minor | - | **extend-skill** - docs-audit is the owner but no check reads the form a doc's assets take - a checked-in binary diagram is neither misfiled, unlinked, nor an undocumented component - and the regenerate-on-merge half becomes a ci-audit `ci/gate-enforcement` question only once such a job already exists. | - |
| [House rule: don't hard-wrap Markdown source](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#house-rule-dont-hard-wrap-markdown-source)<br>Write one paragraph as one line in the Markdown source and let the renderer wrap - never hard-wrap prose to a column and never reflow a code block or a diagram - so a one-word edit stays a one-line diff and the source reads well in tools that soft-wrap. | static | Minor | - | **extend-skill** - mechanically checkable and entirely unmapped - docs-audit is the owner and reads what the docs say and where they sit, never how their source is formatted. | - |
| [Checklist: shipping documentation](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#checklist-shipping-documentation)<br>Eight-item recap for shipping documentation - docs moved in the same pull request as the change, each path, flag, import and cross-link verified against the source, prescriptive content in architecture docs with superseded exploration in research docs cross-linked, the relevant decision-trail artifact present, touched docs reachable from an index with reciprocal links, docstrings updated for any changed purpose or interface, Markdown source not hard-wrapped, and a link-and-index checker guarding it in CI where possible. | process | Important | - | - | A recap, so what it adds is the act of working the list before shipping. Each of the eight items is owned by a Part 8 row above. |
| [See also](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#see-also)<br>Cross-links to Parts 1 and 7 and the handbook index. | informative | - | - | - | - |

## Part 9: Security, dependencies & supply chain

| Section / claim | Class | Severity | Mapped checks | Gap | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [First-party code: trace a path from source to sink](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/security-supply-chain.md#first-party-code-trace-a-path-from-source-to-sink)<br>Report a security finding as a path from an untrusted source to a dangerous sink and name both, counting model and tool outputs as untrusted sources alongside HTTP handlers, CLI arguments, file and object-store reads, message queues and the environment, then neutralize at the sink (parameterized queries, an argument-list subprocess with no shell, safe deserialization, hardened XML) and validate and canonicalize at the boundary (allowlists, path-containment checks, URL-host allowlisting). | static | Critical | `security/injection` / Injection<br>`security/dangerous-calls` / Dangerous calls / code execution<br>`security/unsafe-io` / Unsafe I/O & deserialization | - | The three checks carry the sink taxonomy this section names, and tracing a verified source-to-sink path is the skill's own load-bearing evidence step. The agent-specific source - an LLM or tool output treated as untrusted rather than as trusted data - is declared in the skill's scope section rather than as a check, so it rides along with the checks above rather than being separately citable. |
| [Grant the agent the least privilege it needs](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/security-supply-chain.md#grant-the-agent-the-least-privilege-it-needs)<br>Treat an agent's granted powers as an attack surface in their own right - never concentrate the lethal trifecta of private-data access, untrusted-content exposure and the ability to act on the outside world in one agent without a human gate on the acting edge, default a diagnostic, research or analysis agent to read-only tool and MCP access, and widen write access per tool and per purpose, never wholesale and never to production or the pipeline for convenience. | static | Critical | - | **extend-skill** - security-audit is the owner, since prompt injection as application security is explicitly its surface, but none of its six checks reads an agent's granted tool and MCP surface; ci-audit's `ci/permissions-secrets` is the nearest and scopes least privilege to the pipeline token rather than to what an agent is allowed to do. | - |
| [Secrets: never commit them, and rotate: don't just delete](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/security-supply-chain.md#secrets-never-commit-them-and-rotate-dont-just-delete) (a)<br>Keep no credential in source, defaults, tests, fixtures or notebooks - a secret read from the environment is fine, a secret literal is not. | static | Critical | `security/secrets-in-code` / Secrets in code | - | An exact fit - the check names defaults, tests, fixtures and notebooks in the same breath, and reading the line to tell an environment lookup from a literal is its stated verification step. |
| [Secrets: never commit them, and rotate: don't just delete](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/security-supply-chain.md#secrets-never-commit-them-and-rotate-dont-just-delete) (b)<br>Treat a committed secret as live until rotated - rotate the credential at its provider first, then remove the line, then purge history if it was ever pushed - and never merely suppress this one. | static | Critical | `security/secret-history` / Git-history secret scan | **extend-skill** - partial - `security/secret-history` reaches the part of this claim that was a pure citeability gap when this note was last written, because it scans the full commit history rather than only the working tree, and its review lens asks directly whether a confirmed leak was rotated rather than only deleted, which is the rotate-then-purge half security-audit otherwise only stated outside a citable record (the severity rubric refuses to suppress a confirmed secret and demands rotation, the fix patterns give the rotate-then-remove-then-purge order). Three residues remain. Adoption - the check is opt-in and off by default, so a routine sweep that never enables it never asks the question; security-audit owns that fix, either by promoting the check off opt-in or by stating in its header that a secrets pass is incomplete until the history scan has run, which is why this gap stays extend-skill rather than report-only. Provider-side rotation - as this row's own note records, no check can confirm from a repo snapshot that a flagged rotation actually happened. Detection reach - the scan only sees a secret still present in history, so a team that purges without rotating, the exact merely-suppress move this claim forbids, leaves nothing to flag and the review lens never fires. That third residue is a blind spot rather than the near-miss rule's disqualifier, which refuses a mapping whose check would be *satisfied by* the violation, as an inline model ID satisfies `eval/reproducibility`. On a leak that is still there this check flags it rather than passing it, which is why this row maps with a residue instead of gapping everything. | Rotation at the provider is the half no snapshot can settle - a repo can show that the literal is gone and the history clean, never that the credential was actually retired. |
| [Depend only on what you can account for](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/security-supply-chain.md#depend-only-on-what-you-can-account-for) (a)<br>Know your third-party surface transitively and audit four things - licenses against your own license and distribution model, advisories affecting the resolved versions, freshness (outdated, yanked or end-of-life), and hygiene (declared-but-unused, used-but-undeclared, conflicting pins) - pinning direct dependencies and committing the lockfile as the record of what actually ran. | static | Critical | `deps/licenses` / License compatibility<br>`deps/vulnerabilities` / Known vulnerabilities<br>`deps/freshness` / Freshness<br>`deps/hygiene` / Hygiene | - | An exact fit - the handbook's four axes are deps-audit's four core checks, transitivity is the resolved graph the skill takes as ground truth, and unpinned floating direct dependencies sit inside `deps/freshness`. |
| [Depend only on what you can account for](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/security-supply-chain.md#depend-only-on-what-you-can-account-for) (b)<br>Apply the same rule to the AI surface - treat the model and the provider as dependencies too, pinning model versions where the provider allows it, recording which model produced a given result, and knowing your providers' data-retention terms, because a silent model upgrade is an unpinned dependency that can move your eval numbers out from under you. | static | Important | `eval/reproducibility` / Reproducibility | **extend-skill** - eval-audit's `eval/reproducibility` asks for a pinned, recorded model version and so covers the eval surface exactly; deps-audit is the owner of the wider claim and its inventory is the package graph, so a model or a provider never enters the dependency surface it accounts for. | - |
| [Treat the pipeline as a privileged environment](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/security-supply-chain.md#treat-the-pipeline-as-a-privileged-environment)<br>Treat CI as a privileged runtime holding your secrets as well as the merge gate - default the pipeline token to read-only and widen only the single job that genuinely needs it, pin third-party actions to an immutable commit SHA rather than a mutable tag, never run untrusted pull-request code with secrets in scope, and prefer short-lived federated credentials over long-lived stored secrets. | static | Critical | `ci/permissions-secrets` / Permissions / secrets<br>`ci/action-supply-chain` / Action supply chain<br>`ci/trigger-safety` / Trigger safety | - | The second exact fit in Part 9 - each of the four clauses, federated credentials included, is named inside one of these three checks. |
| [Turn every fix into a gate](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/security-supply-chain.md#turn-every-fix-into-a-gate)<br>Encode each class of safety fix as an executable check wired into CI and pre-commit - a SAST plus secret scan for first-party code, a CVE-plus-license gate for dependencies, a workflow linter and an action-pin checker for the pipeline - because every fix is one-time while the class of problem is forever. | static | Important | `ci/gate-enforcement` / Gate enforcement | **extend-skill** - the same shape and the same owner as Part 1's make-the-standard-executable row, applied to the safety surfaces - ci-audit's `ci/gate-enforcement` audits the gates a project already has, while security-audit and deps-audit detect the available scanners only to choose their own tooling, so no check reports that a repo runs no secret scan and no CVE gate at all, and the pre-commit half is unrepresented anywhere. | - |

Each of the fifteen items is owned by a Part 9 row above. |
