## Part 10: Data protection & privacy

| Section / claim | Class | Severity | Mapped checks | Gap | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Know what personal data you hold, and where it goes](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/data-protection.md#know-what-personal-data-you-hold-and-where-it-goes)<br>Keep a data-flow map beside the code and maintained with it, answering where personal data enters, every store it rests in (primary store, object store, vector index, caches, logs, eval datasets, backups) and every outbound edge that leaves the trust boundary; derive it from the repository rather than from memory, so it is falsifiable against the code. | artifact | Important | - | **new-domain** - #4 - no skill reads for a data-flow map or reconstructs one from the code, and absence of the map is itself the finding rather than a pass; this is squarely the data-protection domain the target issue creates. | - |
| [Every processor needs a legal basis, and the register must match the code](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/data-protection.md#every-processor-needs-a-legal-basis-and-the-register-must-match-the-code) (a)<br>Treat every third party that sees personal data on your behalf as a processor - model APIs, search, OCR, extraction and transcription, hosting and managed databases, and the ones forgotten because they receive prompts rather than documents (tracing and observability backends, error trackers, eval platforms) - and record per processor a signed DPA, whether the provider trains on your data and how you opted out, and the retention window including any longer abuse-monitoring one. | artifact | Critical | - | **new-domain** - #4 - the evidence is a signed agreement and a provider's published terms, both outside the repository entirely; nothing in the family reads either. This row carries the legal-basis claim that used to sit on the Part 9 dependency row. | - |
| [Every processor needs a legal basis, and the register must match the code](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/data-protection.md#every-processor-needs-a-legal-basis-and-the-register-must-match-the-code) (b)<br>Reconcile the register against what the code actually calls - SDK imports, configured base URLs, MCP servers and tool endpoints, the credentials the deployment carries - because a provider reachable from the code and missing from the register is the half of this question a repository can settle, and report it apart from the half it cannot. | static | Critical | - | **new-domain** - #4 - deps-audit's inventory is the package graph, so a provider reached over HTTP never enters it, and no skill derives an outbound-provider list from imports, base URLs or tool endpoints. `security/sensitive-data` reads outbound URL construction, but for exposure at the call site rather than to enumerate who is called. | - |
| [Keep the data where the law lets it be](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/data-protection.md#keep-the-data-where-the-law-lets-it-be)<br>Keep personal data in a permitted region or a destination covered by an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses, and enforce it the way the handbook enforces any environment-selecting value - the region pinned explicitly in configuration, required rather than defaulted, validated at startup and named in the error when missing - then check the places residency is actually lost (provider failover, a store whose region was chosen once at creation, telemetry in another jurisdiction, cross-region backups, a payload copied to a laptop to reproduce a bug). | static | Critical | - | **new-domain** - #4 - a region setting and its absence are both readable from configuration and no skill reads for either; ci-audit's `ci/permissions-secrets` is the nearest thing in the family and scopes to pipeline credentials rather than to where a request lands. The failover and backup cases need deployment facts a repository snapshot does not carry, so they stay unreachable even once the domain exists. | - |
| [Minimize before the boundary](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/data-protection.md#minimize-before-the-boundary)<br>Redact, pseudonymize or truncate personal data before it crosses the trust boundary and prefer a reference over a payload, placing the redaction in the one call path every request goes through rather than at each call site; and settle its quality cost as an eval dimension rather than assuming it away in either direction, because a team that assumes it away ships a regression under a privacy justification. | static | Important | - | **new-domain** - #4 - eval-audit owns whether a behaviour is evaluated and has no dimension for redaction, and no skill reads the outbound call path for a minimization step; the whole claim needs the domain the target issue creates. | - |
| [Retention and deletion are design decisions, not cleanup](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/data-protection.md#retention-and-deletion-are-design-decisions-not-cleanup)<br>Give every store holding personal data a deliberately chosen retention limit that something enforces (a TTL, a lifecycle rule, a scheduled job with a test), and build the deletion path as a feature that walks the data-flow map, because an agentic system's derived copies - embeddings and the vector index, cached model responses, stored traces, run artifacts, eval datasets and fixtures extracted from real cases, backups - are what a deletion reaching only the primary store misses. | static | Critical | - | **new-domain** - #4 - nothing in the family enumerates a project's stores or reads for a retention limit on one, and the derived-copy half depends on the data-flow map this part's first row asks for; this is the domain the target issue creates. | - |
| [Personal data does not belong in the trail](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/data-protection.md#personal-data-does-not-belong-in-the-trail)<br>Keep personal data out of logs, traces, error messages, run artifacts and eval fixtures - log the identifier you can join back rather than the record, keep payloads out of exception messages because an exception travels further than a log line, and build fixtures from synthetic, consented or already-redacted data - because capture-the-trail and data protection reconcile by redacting the payload, not by capturing less. | static | Critical | `security/sensitive-data` / Sensitive-data handling | **new-domain** - #4 - partial - `security/sensitive-data` reads logging and exception-handling call sites near secret- or PII-bearing variables, so it flags the log and error-message half of this claim rather than passing it, which is what the near-miss rule requires of a mapping. The residue is everything that is a stored artifact rather than a call site: traces and run records, eval datasets, and the fixtures extracted from real documents. A first-party-code lens does not read those, and they are the copies that persist longest, so their status needs the domain the target issue creates. | - |
| [Verify against the real artifacts](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/data-protection.md#verify-against-the-real-artifacts)<br>Run the verification counterpart of this part as a standing check over four things - the register against the outbound calls the code makes, the pinned regions against the providers configured, the retention limits against the stores the data-flow map lists, and a scan of logs, fixtures and run artifacts for personal data - report-only first and then one surface at a time; and separate what the repository says is clean from what it cannot see at all, naming each unverifiable item with what would settle it and who holds that evidence. | artifact | Important | - | **new-domain** - #4 - the standing check this row describes is the skill the target issue creates. audit-core already owns the report-only-then-fix cadence and the rule that absence of evidence is never a clean result, and has no lens in this domain to apply them through; the audit cadence itself sits outside every skill's evidence base, as it does on the Part 1 and Part 9 rows that make the same claim. | - |
| [Checklist: a data-protection sweep](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/data-protection.md#checklist-a-data-protection-sweep)<br>Sixteen-item recap in seven groups - the map (it exists beside the code and is falsifiable against it), processors (every third party registered including telemetry and eval platforms, each with a DPA, a training position and a retention window, the register reconciled against the code with the date recorded), residency (region pinned and validated at startup, every outside destination covered by adequacy or SCCs, failover and backups and telemetry checked), minimization (redaction in the shared call path, its quality cost measured), retention and deletion (an enforced limit per store, a deletion path walking the map through the derived copies, and tested), the trail (identifiers not payloads, fixtures synthetic or redacted), and standing (the sweep is run, and its report separates clean from not-visible-from-here). | process | Critical | - | - | A recap, so what it adds is the act of working the list during a sweep. It takes the maximum severity of what it recaps, per the legend's rule for a checklist row, which is the critical band four of this part's rows sit in; each item is owned by a row above. |

## Gap list

Ordered by severity - the risk a violation carries - then by kind, then by handbook order. Each entry names its kind, its recommendation (`extend-skill` / `new-domain` / `report-only`) and, where one exists, the issue that would close it. Three kinds appear, and they are different work: `(unchecked)` is a clause nothing checks, so closing it means new capability; `(residue)` is the part of a claim a mapped check does not reach, so closing it widens something that already runs; `(process)` is a claim no snapshot can settle, which closes in report prose and an adoption roadmap rather than in any skill's matrix. Each band opens with its own split, and a band's unchecked count is the same number as its [cross-tab](#severity-x-coverage) Unmapped column.

### Minor

13 unchecked, 4 residues.

- [`implementation-disciplines/prompt-and-sop-engineering-b`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/implementation-disciplines.md#prompt-and-sop-engineering) (b) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - co-owned - prompt-audit's remediation section already states this rule verbatim as a convention it follows, and eval-audit's `eval/prompt-quality` owns prompt-change hygiene through its missing-versioning-or-changelog clause, but neither actually reads commit messages to verify it, which is the evidence base the delivery-trail domain (#11) would supply.
- [`implementation-disciplines/ci-and-static-analysis-b`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/implementation-disciplines.md#ci-and-static-analysis) (b) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - docs-audit does audit docstrings, now as citable opt-in records (docs/docstring-coverage, docs/docstring-staleness), but each is a genuine near miss rather than full closure: docs/docstring-coverage only tests whether a docstring exists at all, so a one-word placeholder passes it while still failing the quality bar this claim wants, and docs/docstring-staleness only tests contradiction, so a docstring left incomplete after a change contradicts nothing and passes it while still failing the broader staleness this claim asks for; no check asks whether the docstring check itself is wired into the gate. One of three rows stating the docstring rule (with coding-hygiene-rules-that-surface-at-review-d and documentation/keep-the-living-docs-current-too-a), each carrying its own near-miss residue rather than one shared fix.
- [`implementation-disciplines/ci-and-static-analysis-c`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/implementation-disciplines.md#ci-and-static-analysis) (c) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - #5 - ci-audit, prompt-audit and eval-audit are already language-neutral, so a TypeScript project still gets its pipeline, prompt and behavioural audits, and arch, deps, security and test now declare TypeScript tooling beside their Python tooling. What is left is two records that still declare `python:` alone - `arch/martin-metrics` (package stability metrics from a `grimp` graph) and `docs/docstring-coverage` (docstring presence from ruff's `D` rules, pydocstyle or interrogate) - and both set `optin` to true, so a default sweep of a TypeScript partition no longer meets a check with no lens. `tests/scripts/test_audit_checks.py::test_every_tooling_record_offers_a_typescript_lens` asserts that pair by equality, so this note goes stale loudly rather than quietly.
- [`implementation-disciplines/ci-and-static-analysis-d`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/implementation-disciplines.md#ci-and-static-analysis) (d) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - no check flags a review or audit agent pointed at work a deterministic tool already does; prompt-audit is the nearest owner, as on prompt-and-sop-engineering-c.
- [`implementation-disciplines/coding-hygiene-rules-that-surface-at-review-d`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/implementation-disciplines.md#coding-hygiene-rules-that-surface-at-review) (d) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - docstring currency is exactly docs/docstring-staleness's own near miss: that check's detection is contradiction (a docstring actively wrong about parameters, return type, or behaviour), while this claim's 'current with purpose and interface' ask is broader - a docstring left incomplete after a change (a new parameter added but not yet mentioned) contradicts nothing and passes the check while still failing the ask. Not a duplicate of ci-and-static-analysis-b or documentation/keep-the-living-docs-current-too-a despite the shared clause: the two claims either side of it, self-documenting settings fields and provider-safe tool-argument types, have no check anywhere.
- [`codebase-structure/compose-agents-with-typed-hooks-over-a-generic-runner-a`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#compose-agents-with-typed-hooks-over-a-generic-runner) (a) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - arch-audit is the nearest owner, but no check detects plumbing duplicated once per application - the tell is repetition across agents, not a bad import - and its axes point the other way, since a generic runner with one implementer reads as `arch/over-abstraction`, so composition-over-forking stays invisible until the fork produces a cycle or a layering break.
- [`agent-harness/build-the-harness-dont-inline-the-plumbing`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#build-the-harness-dont-inline-the-plumbing) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - arch-audit is the nearest owner but has no check for plumbing duplicated once per agent - the tell is repetition across applications, not a bad import - and nothing audits which tier the reliability defaults live in; the bounding half of the claim is carried by make-bounding-the-default.
- [`agent-harness/resolve-models-through-aliases-never-hard-coded-ids`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#resolve-models-through-aliases-never-hard-coded-ids) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - eval-audit is the owner, since model identity is its surface, but no check scans call sites for inline provider model IDs; its `eval/reproducibility` check is the nearest and wants a run's model version pinned and recorded, which an inline ID satisfies perfectly well - the worked example of the near-miss rule, mapping it would pass exactly what the handbook forbids - and security-audit's `security/secrets-in-code` sees only the credentials half of what the catalog centralizes.
- [`agent-harness/expose-model-parameters-as-optional-defaulted-flags`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/agent-harness.md#expose-model-parameters-as-optional-defaulted-flags) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - eval-audit is the owner, since the generation-parameter surface is exactly what a like-for-like comparison varies one variable at a time, but the section's own claim is wholly unmapped - no check asks whether generation parameters are exposed as optional flags falling back to provider defaults, nor whether a reasoning budget flag exists where the model supports one.
- [`documentation/keep-the-living-docs-current-too-a`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#keep-the-living-docs-current-too) (a) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - This is the fullest of the three docstring rows, and each of its axes is a near miss to a different opt-in record. docs/docstring-standard checks conformance to 'the project's convention', a locally-defined bar that can be weaker than this claim's fixed 'what it does and how to use it' ask. docs/docstring-coverage and docs/docstring-staleness carry the same near misses as the other two docstring rows (an existence bar vs. the quality bar, and contradiction vs. the broader currency ask). Nothing checks whether a docstring fix that resolves one of these actually took the normal code gate rather than the lighter docs-only path. Third of the three docstring rows (with ci-and-static-analysis-b and coding-hygiene-rules-that-surface-at-review-d); the code-gate clause is unique to this row.
- [`documentation/keep-the-living-docs-current-too-c`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#keep-the-living-docs-current-too) (c) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - the same unmapped claim and the same owners as Part 2's prompt-and-sop-engineering row - eval-audit's `eval/prompt-quality` owns prompt-change hygiene through its missing-versioning-or-changelog clause and prompt-audit states the convention in its own remediation section, but neither actually reads commit messages to verify it, which is the evidence base the delivery-trail domain (#11) would supply.
- [`documentation/keep-the-living-docs-current-too-d`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#keep-the-living-docs-current-too) (d) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - docs-audit is the owner but no check reads the form a doc's assets take - a checked-in binary diagram is neither misfiled, unlinked, nor an undocumented component - and the regenerate-on-merge half becomes a ci-audit `ci/gate-enforcement` question only once such a job already exists.
- [`documentation/house-rule-dont-hard-wrap-markdown-source`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#house-rule-dont-hard-wrap-markdown-source) (unchecked) - **extend-skill** - mechanically checkable and entirely unmapped - docs-audit is the owner and reads what the docs say and where they sit, never how their source is formatted.
- [`codebase-structure/point-every-dependency-toward-the-core-and-never-cycle-b`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#point-every-dependency-toward-the-core-and-never-cycle) (b) (residue) - **extend-skill** - arch-audit is the owner, but its `arch/layering` check presupposes that the project has documented its tiers rather than asking whether it has, and no check looks for an import-boundary contract at all; ci-audit's `ci/gate-enforcement` reaches only the case where such a workflow already exists and asks whether it is required.
- [`codebase-structure/dispatch-on-a-discriminator-not-a-type`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/codebase-structure.md#dispatch-on-a-discriminator-not-a-type) (residue) - **extend-skill** - arch-audit is the owner, and the row maps only on the consequence the handbook names, a type-test chain that couples the dispatcher to every concrete class and so breaks a tier boundary; no check flags isinstance/instanceof dispatch as such, nor asks for a single provider-agnostic entry point or declarative per-variant settings resolution. The section is written from a Python vantage (Pydantic discriminated unions, match on a Literal, pydantic-settings per variant); the equivalent TypeScript shape - a discriminated union on a literal tag, switch with exhaustiveness checking, and a schema library resolving env per variant - needs confirming before this row is audited on a TS codebase (#5).
- [`three-layer-model/hold-the-contracts-that-make-layering-pay-off-a`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/three-layer-model.md#hold-the-contracts-that-make-layering-pay-off) (a) (residue) - **extend-skill** - arch-audit is the owner of the anti-corruption boundary, a dependency rule (only the builder may import an engine's schema) it enforces once the project declares it among its layering rules. The representation's own requirements - typed blocks, containment, per-block provenance, engine identity kept out of the block shape - are schema properties no check inspects and no skill is a natural owner of, exactly as on hold-the-contracts-that-make-layering-pay-off-b; that residue is report prose against Part 4's checklist.
- [`documentation/audit-docs-like-a-test-suite-b`](https://github.com/mesagroup/ai-agent-development-handbook/blob/main/docs/engineering/documentation.md#audit-docs-like-a-test-suite) (b) (residue) - **extend-skill** - `ci/gate-enforcement` asks whether a checker that exists is actually required, so a project with no checker at all passes it; docs-audit is the owner and treats the checker as a deliverable it may propose rather than as a check it scores.

### Severity x coverage

The actionable question: which high-risk clauses does nothing check? The Unmapped column is the answer, and the rows behind each count are listed by name, tagged `(unchecked)`, under the matching heading in the [gap list](#gap-list) above. Read a Critical unmapped count as the head of the queue. The four data columns before the Process one count auditable rows only; the Process column counts rows that carry a severity but can never be checked from a snapshot, and so belong in report prose and an adoption roadmap rather than in any skill's matrix.

| Severity | Fully mapped | Partial | Unmapped | Auditable total | Process |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | 4 | 2 | 6 | 12 | 5 |
| Important | 15 | 17 | 33 | 65 | 15 |
| Minor | 2 | 4 | 13 | 19 | 2 |

135 rows total. Of the 96 auditable rows (74 static + 22 artifact): **21 fully mapped** (22%), **23 partially mapped** (a check that reaches part of the claim, with the residue recorded as a gap), and **52 unmapped** (no check reaches the claim; every one of them still carries a gap entry saying so and why, which the schema requires). All 75 gap entries sit on auditable rows: the 52 unmapped ones plus the 23 partial. The remaining 22 process and 17 informative rows are not auditable by design - the honest record of what a snapshot cannot settle.
